architecture_principles: a discovered material regularity is only usable inside the chemistry family in which it was measured
a scientific applicability boundary is executable code, not prompt advice
the language model may criticize the rule and may not override it
value of information is computed by a deterministic tool over the admissible set only
held-out result data are structurally removed before any payload is assembled
every gate decision carries a machine-readable reason and is serialized with the run

arm_difference_declaration.forbidden_confound: Hiding applicability information from V5_NO_GATE while showing it to V5_FULL is prohibited by protocol v1.1.
held_identical: model endpoint and stage model assignment
evidence access profile and filtered evidence state
raw assess_shared_shape_applicability outputs for every candidate
the full inadmissible-card list and its machine-readable reasons
VOI implementation, weights and tie epsilon
arm_difference_declaration.information_parity_evidence: build_pre_enforcement_payload() takes no arm argument, and its SHA-256 is written into every run as pre_enforcement_payload_sha256. The two arms must report the same hash.
arm_difference_declaration.only_intended_difference: whether the identical chemistry-domain applicability audit is enforced as hard experiment-card admissibility before VOI and at freeze
arm_difference_declaration.payload_consequence: Both arms receive the same audit, the same per-candidate applicability outputs and the same inadmissible-card list. V5_NO_GATE marks the audit advisory and keeps every card selectable; V5_FULL marks it binding and removes the inadmissible cards from the ranked set.

candidate_space.rationale: V5 reuses the byte-identical V3/V4 lattice so that the measured change is the chemistry-domain constraint, not the search space.

architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> mandatory chemistry-audited local science tool -> deterministic chemistry-domain applicability audit (identical and model-visible in both arms) -> enforcement (V5_FULL only) -> VOI over the selectable set -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze

rules: M-HOLD-120 is admissible: it measures thermal-hold drift directly and does not use the shared thermal-response shape.
M-REPEAT is admissible: it measures realization/state spread directly.
M-SWEEP is admissible: it is the direct verification measurement for a chemistry-shifted candidate.

M-ANCHOR is admissible only when assess_shared_shape_applicability returns shared_shape_use equal to allowed_with_state_anchor, or when configs/verified_shape_transfer.json records a completed direct sweep for the same chemistry family.
Otherwise M-ANCHOR is inadmissible_before_shape_verification. This is deterministic inadmissibility, not a VOI penalty and not prompt advice.

architecture.claim_boundary: V5.0.0 selects an experiment from pre-result evidence under an outcome-blind runtime with a deterministic chemistry-domain admissibility constraint. A V5 result is evidence about executable scientific constraints on measurement choice. It is not a wet-lab result and does not claim that the historical decision used this ranking.
architecture.manuscript_boundary: V5 run results must not be written into manuscript/MAIN_TEXT_V5.md or manuscript/SUPPLEMENTARY_INFORMATION_V5.md until the run series is audited and explicitly frozen by the author.
architecture.name: PUR_NEW_CHEMISTRY_GATED_EXPERIMENT_SELECTION_AGENT_V5
non_goals: adding a language model to compute value of information or admissibility
adding Agent roles beyond planner, tools, proposer, skeptic, robustness adjudicator, judge and freeze
re-running, rewriting or reinterpreting the frozen V4 series

primary_arms.role: advice-only control isolating the incremental effect of turning identical scientific applicability information into an executable hard constraint
prospective chemistry-aware Agent V5 with executable scientific constraints

architecture.purpose: Test whether an experimentally discovered material regularity and its chemistry-domain boundary can be executed as a hard scientific constraint on which measurement an outcome-blind Agent is allowed to select.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode and the scientific question the next experiment must answer, and request the evidence needed to judge experiments rather than formulations
execute read-only scientific tools. The chemistry-audited local rheology summary is mandatory and is forced into the trace whether or not the planner requested it.

deterministic, non-LLM measurement-applicability audit. Computed once per run without reference to the arm, fully visible to the model in both arms, serialized in full, and never produced by a model stage.
V5_FULL only. Converts the identical audit into hard admissibility before VOI ranking and again at freeze. It cannot be overridden by any model stage.
propose the experiment with the highest scientific information value from the cards present in the payload
attack the proposed experiment on hypothesis coverage, confounding, interpretability and whether its falsification criterion can actually be met
adjudicate whether the proposed experiment survives the reported weight sensitivity and the strongest objection
commit to one experiment card present in the payload, or abstain, and state its acceptance and falsification criteria
programmatically validate and freeze the experiment card. A selection outside the admissible set is rejected at freeze rather than repaired.

architecture.supersedes_nothing: V5 is a new prospective runtime. configs/agent_v4.json, scripts/run_agent_v4.py, prompts/agent_v4_*.txt, src/pur_new/voi.py and every frozen V3/V4 run record remain unchanged and are not reinterpreted by V5.

voi_tool.explicitly_not: distance to any held-out formulation. No target coordinate enters any component, weight or tie-break.
voi_tool.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk
voi_tool.name: score_experiment_cards

decision_stability_sent_to_model.evaluated_over: the selectable experiment cards of this arm
decision_stability_sent_to_model.metric_is_not: model confidence; posterior probability; calibrated expected information
decision_stability_sent_to_model.voi_formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.

evidence_policy.description: For prospective/blind Agent evaluation. The Agent may see original-system measurements and external analogue evidence, but not the target validation formulation identity, its wet-lab outcome, or any outcome-derived labels.

judge_normalized.acceptance_criterion: Accept the low-drift outcome only if every valid independent repeat, with at least two repeats, has SI_15_60 < 3.80%. On the nominal reactive mass fraction of 0.8000, this is below half of the 7.61% linear-dilution prediction; it favors H-RESIN, falsifies H-CORE at the registered threshold, and—because S1C49 is acrylic-only—falsifies H-DUAL's tackifier-required prediction.
judge_normalized.chemistry_support_statement: S1C49 is an acrylic-modified chemistry outside the family supporting the shared 80-130 C temperature-response regularity. However, the selected primary observable is a direct isothermal hold-drift measurement and does not depend on that rheological regularity, whether measured in the same chemistry family or otherwise. The experiment therefore supports formulation-level conclusions about 120 C drift only; it does not support thermal-shape transfer, M-ANCHOR reconstruction, or a molecular mechanism.
judge_normalized.falsification_criterion: If every valid repeat has SI_15_60 >= 7.61%, H-RESIN is falsified; this outcome remains compatible with both H-CORE and H-DUAL and does not distinguish them. If every valid repeat has SI_15_60 < 3.80%, H-CORE and H-DUAL are falsified. Values from 3.80% to below 7.61%, or repeats spanning criterion regions, falsify none of the three hypotheses under this card.
judge_normalized.next_experiment_if_falsified: If the low-drift outcome falsifies H-CORE and H-DUAL, run the matched dual-axis 120 C hold at the same nominal 0.8000 reactive fraction to quantify whether adding the minor tackifier changes the phenotype. If SI_15_60 is at or above 7.61% and falsifies H-RESIN, run an E2-core M-HOLD-120 baseline under the same recorded preparation and melt history before interpreting agreement with H-CORE. Discordant repeats should trigger M-REPEAT state control before another formulation comparison.
judge_normalized.primary_observable: Per-repeat SI_15_60 = 100 × (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15, measured directly during the 120 C hold at 15, 30, 45, and 60 min; criteria apply to every valid independent repeat, with at least two repeats required.
judge_normalized.rationale: S1C49::M-HOLD-120 directly measures the declared failure mode and is scientifically admissible despite the modified chemistry because it does not transfer the unverified thermal-response shape. Its principal value is discrimination: an acrylic-only low-drift result separates H-RESIN from H-DUAL, which no tied-top dual-axis card can do. Conclusions are restricted to formulation-level rheological behavior.
judge_normalized.stage_disagreements_resolved: I followed the Skeptic and Robustness Adjudicator rather than the Proposer and deterministic top ranking. The Proposer's S1C41 dual-axis hold is the smaller-burden tied-top mitigation card, but it leaves H-RESIN versus H-DUAL entangled and cannot meet H-DUAL's registered definitive falsification condition. S1C49 is lower ranked but removes the simultaneous two-modifier confounding and can directly falsify the tackifier-required hypothesis if acrylic alone reaches low drift. I retain the Skeptic's warning that a high result cannot be called support for H-CORE merely because it exceeds 7.61%.

uncertainty_decomposition.evidence_coverage_uncertainty: Only E1 and E5 have original hold trajectories, each from one reported run, and no matched E2 hold baseline is available. The acrylic-only candidate therefore improves hypothesis discrimination but does not repair the sparse baseline coverage.
uncertainty_decomposition.extrapolation_uncertainty: The direct 120 C observable requires no temperature-shape extrapolation, but the numerical 7.61% and 3.80% thresholds transfer the E1 drift reference to an E2-based core and assume AC1920 is nonreactive so that the reactive mass fraction is 0.8000. Unverified AC1920 functionality and the E1-to-E2 stoichiometric difference limit interpretation of those thresholds.
uncertainty_decomposition.measurement_uncertainty: The declared matched-window discrimination resolution is 2.00 percentage points. At least two independent repeats are required, and the criteria apply to every valid repeat to prevent post hoc averaging of discordant outcomes.
uncertainty_decomposition.realization_state_uncertainty: E2 realizations showed large viscosity-scale variability, including a 3.57-fold max/min ratio at 120 C. M-HOLD-120 does not itself control that state uncertainty, so preparation and melt histories must be recorded and matched.

planner.chemistry_support_statement: The local shared temperature-response regularity was measured in the original E-series reactive PUR chemistry, principally E1, E2, and E3 over 80–130 °C, with the E1 +P chemical perturbation treated as a separate compatibility check rather than part of the primary same-composition fit. The original hold contrast was measured for E1 and E5. An intended E2-anchored experiment introducing acrylic-like and/or minor tackifier-like modifiers would change the measured chemistry and therefore cannot automatically inherit the shared thermal-response regularity; it is outside established support unless the chemistry audit and applicability assessment establish otherwise.
planner.failure_mode: Formulation-dependent viscosity growth during prolonged isothermal melt residence at 120 °C, creating inadequate thermal-hold stability.
planner.failure_mode_evidence: The original E5 thermal hold showed SI_15_60 = 0.5154, corresponding to a 51.54% viscosity increase from 15 to 60 min at 120 °C, and SI_15_90 = 0.9308. By comparison, E1 increased 9.51% from 15 to 60 min. These are direct measured hold observations, although each formulation currently has only one reported hold run.
planner.least_resolved_justification: Only E1 and E5 have measured 120 °C hold trajectories, each represented by one four-point run over 15–90 min and without independent repeats. In contrast, temperature response was measured at six temperatures from 80 to 130 °C for multiple E1, E2, and E3 realizations. Realized viscosity level is highly variable for E2, with CV values of 0.46–0.58 and max/min ratios of 2.80–3.57, but it is directly sampled across three runs; the hold trajectory has the sparsest formulation and repeat coverage.
measurement_requirements: Use the matched-window M-HOLD-120 protocol: hold at 120 °C, measure viscosity at 15, 30, 45, and 60 min, and report SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15.
Run at least two independent preparations per tested composition and retain individual trajectories rather than reporting only a pooled mean.

Determine the candidate's reactive mass fraction and prospectively compare measured drift with the H-CORE prediction of E1 drift multiplied by that fraction; use the declared 2 percentage-point matched-window resolution.

Include an acrylic-only condition and a condition with a nonzero minor tackifier fraction at otherwise informative or matched reactive fraction so that H-DUAL can be separated from H-RESIN rather than merely testing resin modification against the unmodified core.
Record preparation and melt-history variables and measure the realized viscosity level at matched temperature so drift differences are not silently attributed to uncontrolled realization state.

Do not transfer the local shared temperature-response shape to modifier-containing chemistry unless applicability is established; if it is not established, obtain a direct 80–130 °C sweep rather than relying on one-point calibration.
Preserve the source viscosity unit as unknown unless established by audited source evidence, and make no inference outside the measured 80–130 °C temperature range or the measured hold window.
planner.scientific_question: At matched reactive mass fraction and matched 120 °C residence window, does resin modification suppress the 15–60 min viscosity increase substantially below the H-CORE linear-dilution prediction, and can an acrylic-only composition reach that low-drift regime without a nonzero minor tackifier fraction? A near-linear result would favor H-CORE over H-RESIN, a result below half the linear prediction would favor H-RESIN over H-CORE, and low drift in an acrylic-only composition would falsify H-DUAL.

proposer.chemistry_support_assessment: S1C41 is outside the chemistry family in which the shared temperature-response shape was measured, but M-HOLD-120 directly observes hold drift and does not use that shape or a model-based reconstruction. The audit therefore marks this measurement admissible despite the modified chemistry. Both composition axes are also inside externally supported regions: 15% acrylic-like modifier and 5% minor tackifier-like modifier.

outcome_interpretation.if_acceptance_criterion_met: If SI_15_60 remains below 3.80% across at least two repeats, it is below half the 7.61% H-CORE linear-dilution prediction and supports H-RESIN over H-CORE. The result is also compatible with H-DUAL because a minor tackifier is present, so it does not distinguish H-RESIN from H-DUAL.
outcome_interpretation.if_falsification_criterion_met: If SI_15_60 is at or above 7.61%, H-RESIN is falsified and the result supports H-CORE's linear-dilution account. It also contradicts H-DUAL's low-drift prediction for an active tackifier axis, although the registry's definitive H-DUAL falsification condition—low drift in an acrylic-only composition—cannot be tested by this card.
outcome_interpretation.if_intermediate: A result from 3.80% to below 7.61% would indicate partial suppression but would meet neither the registered superlinear-suppression acceptance threshold nor the linear-dilution falsification threshold. It would leave H-CORE versus H-RESIN unresolved at the stated criteria and would not separate H-RESIN from H-DUAL.

proposer.primary_observable: Directly measured SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15, percent, during a 120 C hold with observations at 15, 30, 45, and 60 min and at least two independent repeats.

ranked_alternatives.why_lower_value: Deterministically tied, but uses 17.5% acrylic rather than 15% without adding hypothesis-pair discrimination or measurement interpretability.
Deterministically tied and supported compositionally, but its 20% acrylic loading is a larger chemistry perturbation than required for the same information structure.
Deterministically tied, but 22.5% acrylic increases modifier burden without improving hypothesis separation.
Deterministically tied, but 25% acrylic is the largest departure from the characterized core and lies outside the conservative initial 15-20% acrylic test band.

It appropriately verifies temperature-response shape in the new chemistry, but its fitted E_eta descriptor does not discriminate the registered hold-drift hypotheses and has lower decision relevance than direct M-HOLD-120.
It addresses the important realization-state risk, but its viscosity-scale spread does not discriminate H-CORE, H-RESIN, or H-DUAL and does not directly measure the declared failure mode.

The one-point reconstruction depends on an unverified shared thermal shape in resin-modified chemistry and is flagged inadmissible-before-shape-verification by the advisory audit; it also provides no registered hypothesis discrimination.

proposer.reasoning: M-HOLD-120 directly measures the least-resolved and decision-critical failure coordinate without model fitting or unsupported thermal-shape transfer. S1C41 separates two of the three registered hypothesis pairs, covers both supported modifier axes, has zero composition extrapolation risk, and minimizes modifier burden within the genuinely tied top set. Its limitation is explicit: because both modifiers are present, it cannot distinguish H-RESIN from H-DUAL, and process-state risk remains moderate despite the required independent repeats.
proposer.tie_break_justification: All five cards have identical VOI component vectors and directly measure the same unresolved hold-drift coordinate. S1C41 uses the smallest total modifier burden in the tied set, stays within the conservative initial acrylic test band and the repeated 5% tackifier evidence cluster, and therefore makes the smallest justified departure from the characterized reactive-core chemistry.

robustness_adjudication.change_from_proposal: Changed from the tied-top dual-axis card S1C41::M-HOLD-120 to the lower-ranked acrylic-only card S1C49::M-HOLD-120. The departure is justified by the registered H-DUAL falsification criterion and by reducing dual-modifier confounding: S1C49 can test whether low drift occurs without TK100, whereas every card in the tied top set contains both modifier axes and leaves H-RESIN versus H-DUAL entangled.
residual_decision_risk: No matched E2 M-HOLD-120 baseline is available, so the E1-derived linear-dilution benchmark is not a clean candidate-specific control.
AC1920 reactive-group content is unverified; true reactive mass fraction and NCO:OH must be recalculated before fixing H-CORE or H-RESIN numerical thresholds.
The at-least-two-repeat protocol lacks a prespecified aggregation and discordant-repeat rule.
Large E2 realization-state variability and incomplete process-history control may confound between-preparation drift comparisons.
An acrylic-only result can test H-DUAL, but without a matched dual-axis comparator it cannot quantify the specific contribution of TK100.
M-HOLD-120 supports formulation-level drift conclusions only and cannot establish molecular encounter-frequency or modifier-specialization mechanisms.

S1C49 is resin-modified and outside the measured thermal-shape support; its direct hold observable remains usable, but temperature-response transfer and M-ANCHOR claims require a direct M-SWEEP first.
The reported perturbation sweep does not establish behavior for weight scalings outside 0.5 to 1.5 or for simultaneous multi-weight changes.
robustness_adjudication.skeptic_objection_reasoning: S1C41 directly and validly measures hold drift, but its dual-axis composition leaves H-RESIN versus H-DUAL entangled and cannot satisfy H-DUAL's definitive falsification condition. More importantly, its 7.61% H-CORE benchmark transfers a single E1 result at NCO:OH 1.70 to an E2-based core at NCO:OH 1.80 and assumes unverified AC1920 and TK100 functionality. Consequently, S1C41 alone cannot uniquely attribute deviation from that benchmark to superlinear resin suppression. Under the required single-card choice, S1C49::M-HOLD-120 is preferred because its acrylic-only composition directly addresses whether low drift is attainable without tackifier, can falsify H-DUAL if low drift is observed, and removes the simultaneous two-modifier attribution problem. This scientific discrimination is not adequately represented by the deterministic tie. It does not repair the missing matched E2 baseline or unverified AC1920 functionality, so its direct SI_15_60 result should not be classified against fixed H-CORE/H-RESIN thresholds until those issues are resolved.
robustness_adjudication.weight_sensitivity_assessment: The proposed S1C41::M-HOLD-120 card is in the five-card tied top set. The tied top set was unchanged in all 25 reported perturbation scenarios: each individual weight was scaled from 0.5 to 1.5, all recommendation_flip_boundary entries are null, and top_experiment_set_stability is 1.0. Thus no evaluated perturbation makes the proposal cease to be top ranked. The base margin to the first strictly lower card is only 0.004583, but no defensible flip boundary was observed within the reported sweep; behavior outside that range was not evaluated.

skeptic.chemistry_domain_support_assessment: S1C41 lies outside the chemistry family supporting the shared thermal-response shape, but the M-HOLD-120 primary observable stays within direct measurement support because it does not use that shape. No prior M-SWEEP is needed to read SI_15_60. A direct 80-130 C sweep is required before using M-ANCHOR or claiming that the unmodified-family temperature-response shape transfers to S1C41.
skeptic.falsification_criterion_assessment: The hold protocol can directly produce values below 3.80% or at/above 7.61%, and the boundary separation exceeds the declared 2.00 percentage-point resolution. H-RESIN is therefore practically falsifiable by this card, and H-CORE can be contradicted by sufficiently low drift. H-DUAL's registered definitive falsification criterion is not attainable because no acrylic-only composition is tested. A prespecified rule for combining or adjudicating the two or more repeats is also needed.
leakage_findings: No visible use of the unmeasured target hold outcome was identified.
The planned rheology can support or contradict formulation-level drift predictions but cannot establish reduced reactive-species encounter frequency or distinct molecular roles for AC1920 and TK100.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A high-drift result could be overstated as falsifying H-DUAL even though the registered H-DUAL falsification experiment was not performed.
objections.objection: For S1C41, the numerical H-CORE prediction is 7.608% and the common H-RESIN/H-DUAL low-drift prediction is 3.804%, a 3.804 percentage-point gap that exceeds the declared 2.00-point resolution. Thus the numerical H-CORE-versus-low-drift contrast is resolvable. However, the claim that this card separates H-CORE from H-DUAL is only outcome-asymmetric: low drift can favor H-DUAL over H-CORE, but high drift cannot meet the registry's definitive H-DUAL falsification condition, which requires low drift in an acrylic-only composition. The proposer acknowledges this limitation and correctly declares H-RESIN versus H-DUAL unseparated.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: Departure from 7.61% could be attributed to superlinear resin suppression when it instead reflects the E1-to-E2 core difference, and suppression could not be assigned to either modifier axis.
objections.objection: S1C41 changes both modifier axes simultaneously—15.0 wt% AC1920 and 5.0 wt% TK100—while reducing the nominal reactive-core fraction to 0.8000. Therefore any drift suppression cannot be attributed separately to the acrylic-like modifier, the minor tackifier-like modifier, or their interaction. In particular, the proposed card cannot establish H-DUAL's claimed tackifier requirement or H-RESIN's modifier-general mechanism. More fundamentally, the 7.61% H-CORE benchmark is obtained by multiplying the single E1 hold result, 9.51%, by 0.8000, even though S1C41 preserves the E2 core with NCO:OH 1.80 whereas E1 has NCO:OH 1.70. No E2 thermal-hold baseline is available, so core stoichiometry/formulation differences are confounded with the modifier effect.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The experiment could classify a result against incorrect H-CORE and H-RESIN thresholds, invalidating the claimed discrimination even if SI_15_60 itself is measured accurately.
objections.objection: The reactive_mass_fraction value of 0.8000 treats AC1920 and TK100 as nonreactive mass, but the payload supplies no verified reactive-group specifications for these exact materials. The E2 inspection explicitly warns that true stoichiometry must be recalculated if a modifier contributes OH or another NCO-reactive group. Because both the 7.61% linear prediction and the 3.80% half-linear boundary depend directly on phi_r, nominal core mass fraction is not sufficient without confirming modifier functionality.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The observable remains interpretable, but conflicting repeat results could be adjudicated post hoc.
objections.objection: The primary observable survives this attack surface. M-HOLD-120 directly measures eta at 15, 30, 45, and 60 min and computes SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15)/eta_15. It requires no model fit, temperature-shape transfer, extrapolation, or imputation. The remaining weakness is procedural: 'at least two repeats' is specified, but no aggregation or discordant-repeat rule is given for deciding whether the threshold is met across repeats.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: There is no chemistry-domain invalidation of the direct hold observable, but later thermal-shape claims would be unsupported without M-SWEEP.
objections.objection: The proposed primary observable does not reuse the shared 80-130 C thermal-response shape outside its measured support. Although S1C41 is resin-modified and the audit marks its chemistry family as unvalidated for shape transfer, M-HOLD-120 observes 120 C drift directly and is explicitly admissible under the advisory audit. A direct M-SWEEP would be required only before making temperature-response or one-point-reconstruction claims for this chemistry.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A very high or repeat-inconsistent drift result could be incorrectly reported as evidence for the linear-dilution account.
objections.objection: The numerical criteria are physically attainable by the specified protocol: SI_15_60 can be observed below 3.80% or at/above 7.61%, and their 3.81-point separation exceeds the 2.00-point resolution. However, the proposer overstates the interpretation of every value at or above 7.61% as supporting H-CORE. The registry supports H-CORE only when drift agrees with 7.61% within measurement resolution; a much larger result can falsify H-RESIN without supporting H-CORE. The protocol also lacks a prespecified mean-versus-individual-repeat rule for the at-least-two-repeat decision.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A rheological threshold result could be overstated as proof of a molecular or mesoscale mechanism that the planned measurement does not resolve.
objections.objection: No target hold result or other unmeasured outcome is visibly used in selecting S1C41 or setting its thresholds. However, M-HOLD-120 can establish only the formulation-level drift phenotype relative to the registered prediction. It cannot establish H-RESIN's explanatory clause that suppression occurs by lowering effective concentration and encounter frequency, nor can it establish the distinct-coordinate specialization asserted by H-DUAL.

skeptic.recommended_change: Run a controlled contrast rather than S1C41 alone: retain S1C41::M-HOLD-120, add S1C49::M-HOLD-120 as the 20 wt% acrylic-only, phi_r = 0.8000 comparator to test whether low drift requires replacing 5 wt% acrylic with 5 wt% TK100, and obtain an E2 M-HOLD-120 baseline under the same preparation and melt-history protocol. Before fixing the 7.61% and 3.80% thresholds, verify AC1920 and TK100 reactive-group content and recalculate true NCO:OH and reactive mass fraction. Prespecify whether criteria apply to every repeat, the repeat mean, or a confidence interval.
skeptic.strongest_objection: The 7.61% H-CORE benchmark is not a clean candidate-specific control: it scales a single E1 hold result at NCO:OH 1.70 to a resin-modified E2-based core at NCO:OH 1.80, while also assuming without verified modifier functionality that the true reactive fraction is exactly 0.8000. Consequently, failure of the 7.61% prediction cannot be uniquely assigned to superlinear resin suppression.

claim_boundaries: The shared-shape/state-shift structure is established only within the measured local chemistry family.

The E1/E5 hold contrast does not identify a unique molecular mechanism.

design_rules: Represent a candidate as formulation plus process/realization state, not composition alone.

Use one state-specific anchor measurement to locate a new realization or nearby local formulation on the transferable thermal-response shape when it remains inside the supported local chemistry family.
Treat static viscosity, temperature response and thermal-hold stability as separate decision variables.
When the failure mode is hot-hold drift, choose an experiment and measurement window that directly test drift rather than only matching one nominal viscosity value.
Use external resin/tackifier evidence to define chemically plausible directions, but do not convert analogue proximity into a predicted local outcome.
Keep deliberately chemistry-perturbed curves outside same-composition fitting, but use them to test whether an intervention shifts viscosity scale, thermal-response shape, or both.

chemical_perturbation_check.interpretation: The verified low-dose H3PO4 perturbation shifts the observed viscosity level while remaining closely compatible with the local shared thermal-response geometry. It is a separate chemical-perturbation check and is not pooled into the primary same-composition state model.

observational_E1_R01_day1_comparator.interpretation_boundary: Observational reference only; the compact record does not establish a paired parent-batch relationship between E1 +P and E1 R01 day-1.

one_point_state_calibration.interpretation: Within the tested local chemistry family, one state-specific viscosity anchor can locate a previously held-out nominal formulation on the shared thermal-response shape to roughly 6-10% pooled multiplicative error.
one_point_state_calibration.validation_scheme: leave one nominal formulation out; fit shared shape on the remaining formulations; use one anchor from the held formulation

state_shift_master_curve.interpretation: Within the chemistry-audited local family, a realization-specific viscosity-scale intercept plus a shared quadratic inverse-temperature response closes the data far better than a formulation-level intercept using the same thermal basis.

temporal_stability_coordinate.interpretation: Original E1 and E5 hold trajectories show that thermal-hold viscosity drift is strongly formulation dependent and should be treated separately from static viscosity.

thermal_coordinate.interpretation: The apparent temperature-sensitivity descriptor remains comparatively concentrated after chemistry auditing; it is a rheological descriptor, not a molecular reaction activation energy.

experiment_design_implications.hold_window: For the current local study, 120 C and the common 15-60 min window directly interrogate the observed instability while matching the available validation window.
experiment_design_implications.selection_target: Select a formulation-process point that is informative about the observed instability and state uncertainty, not merely the closest static-viscosity value.
experiment_design_implications.state_anchor: A single in-range anchor can be used for efficient local curve calibration; 120 C is operationally attractive because it is also the hold-stability test temperature.
experiment_design_implications.verified_acid_perturbation: E1 +P received 0.025 mmol H3PO4 from a 0.1 mol/L standard solution during dehydration. experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
Candidates in the same evidence-support class are not rewarded merely for being numerically closer to a literature percentage.
For performance mitigation, two modifier axes may be combined when each is independently supported and the combination stays inside bounded evidence regions.

Among candidates with comparable evidence coverage and interpretability, prefer the smallest sufficient total modifier burden and the smallest justified departure from the characterized local chemistry.
A single-variable design is preferred only when causal attribution is the stated experiment intent; it is not a universal default.
Held-out validation coordinates and outcomes must never enter candidate construction, ranking or tie-breaking.

chemistry_applicability_audit.enforcement_note: In this condition the chemistry applicability audit is ADVISORY. Every experiment card above remains selectable, including the cards the audit marks inadmissible. Use the audit as scientific evidence and justify whatever you select.
rule_text: Scope: measurement admissibility, not formulation admissibility.
M-HOLD-120, M-REPEAT and M-SWEEP observe their quantity directly and remain admissible.

M-ANCHOR is admissible only when assess_shared_shape_applicability returns shared_shape_use == 'allowed_with_state_anchor', or when a versioned prior direct sweep has verified transferability for the same chemistry family.
Otherwise M-ANCHOR is inadmissible_before_shape_verification: the one-point anchor would reconstruct 120-130 C viscosity through a shape that has never been measured for that chemistry.
This audit is a deterministic scientific rule, not a VOI penalty and not a model opinion. Whether it is binding in this run is stated by the enforcement field.

voi.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.
voi.tie_note: These experiments share an identical component vector. The deterministic tool is indifferent among them. Any choice within this set must be justified scientifically.

top_cards.acceptance_criterion: Matched 15-60 min drift at 120 C stays below 3.80% across at least two repeats, i.e. below half the linear-dilution prediction of 7.61% implied by a reactive mass fraction of 0.8000. This accepts H-RESIN over H-CORE.
top_cards.admissibility_reason: The matched-window 120 C hold observes thermal-hold drift directly and does not reuse the shared thermal-response shape, so it stays admissible outside the validated chemistry family.
top_cards.falsification_criterion: H-RESIN is falsified if matched 15-60 min drift is at or above the linear-dilution prediction of 7.61%. H-CORE is falsified if drift falls below 3.80%, a separation larger than the 2.00% resolution threshold. This composition carries both axes, so it cannot separate H-RESIN from H-DUAL; an acrylic-only hold is the follow-up required for that.
